notes.author: agent:claude
notes.text: Registration exists only in the dashboard, so an agent, a provisioning script, or a headless host cannot add a project. The product brief already commits to project add, project list, config path, and doctor; only the config commands exist today.

problem: Registering, listing, and removing projects is possible only through the web dashboard. A coding agent, a setup script, or a headless machine therefore cannot bring a project under control-plane management without a human opening a browser, which contradicts the agent-oriented direction of the reservation and MCP work.
scope: Add project add <path>, project list, and project remove <id> commands that call the existing control services rather than reimplementing registration, detection, or persistence.

Support assigning or auto-selecting a stable port, reusing the existing package-manager and framework detection, and rejecting a repository without a dev script with the same error semantics the dashboard uses.
Add the doctor command promised by the brief so a fresh installation can be verified without the dashboard.
Keep the commands operable while a controller instance is running by routing through the running controller or by refusing clearly when the database is owned by another process.
title: Manage projects from the CLI
validation: Register a repository with project add on a machine with no browser, then confirm the dashboard and list_projects report the same project, port, and detected command.
Verify project add rejects a path that is not a Git repository and a repository without a dev script, in the operating-system locale, without leaving a partial record.
Verify project remove releases the port, stops an owned process tree if one is running, and records an audit event.
Run the commands while a controller owns the database and confirm either correct delegation or an explicit refusal, never a corrupted or concurrently written database.
value: An agent or a provisioning script can bring a project under management end to end, which is a precondition for the unattended workflows the MCP interface is built for.
